findings.cause: checked_file first checks lstat for a regular file, then calls os.open with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC but without O_NONBLOCK. A path replaced with a FIFO between those calls blocks in open before the closing identity checks or any frame watchdog.
findings.impact: The helper may remain blocked before readiness or during later custody reads. The outer driver can refuse/return UNKNOWN while the helper remains alive; file stability checks after reading cannot resolve an open that never returns. No false semantic success or provider effect was demonstrated.
findings.proof: An isolated inert subprocess replaced a regular public fixture with a FIFO exactly inside the open hook, then called the real original os.open. The exact candidate did not return within the one-second harness timeout and was terminated. The same controlled race with only O_NONBLOCK supplied by the test hook refused INPUT_CHANGED in about0.046s. The candidate source was not modified.
findings.required_correction: Add O_NONBLOCK to the wrapper open, inspect the opened descriptor with fstat before reading and require regular-file/full identity equality with the selected pre-open file, and retain the existing after-read and named-path identity checks. Add regular-file, FIFO-race and changed-read regression coverage; do not relax inherited original semantics or retry any actual subject.
findings.title: Blocking open can hang before file-identity and deadline checks
